clue.text: Commotion made by drunk, mostly, crossing border

indicators.note: crossing means the shortened drunk word straddles the edge word, holding it inside
mostly means the slang word for drunk loses its final letter

parts.note: sozzled is slang for drunk
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A drunkard staggering over a boundary line causes a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a noun for a drinker, but it is the adjective, here the slang SOZZLED, which 'mostly' cuts short and which 'crossing' wraps round the edge word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shemozzle is slang for a muddle or rumpus, a noisy confusion.

clue.text: Rascal's humorous retort about Conservative wit

indicators.note: about means the retort word goes around the abbreviation for the party

parts.note: a sally is a witty or humorous retort
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A rogue makes a jokey comeback about a Tory comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rascal's' is read as 'Rascal is', a possessive-looking link that leaves the definition as the bare noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous person or rogue, a synonym for rascal.

clue.text: Make into law, upsetting an Eastern court

indicators.note: upsetting signals that the gathered letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Passing legislation disrupts an Oriental tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a bill is to pass it so it becomes a statute.

clue.text: In old-fashioned style, dismissed fourth form?

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a mode is a form or manner
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A pupil from the fourth-year class has been expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: In schools a 'fourth form' is a year group, but here 'fourth' is D, the fourth letter, and 'form' is MODE; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outmoded is no longer in fashion, so it is dated.

clue.text: Appearing in belt, like 19, for example

definitions.meaning: the zodiac is the belt of sky through which the sun, moon and planets move
19 is the goat, Capricorn, one of the twelve signs of that belt

explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' suggests clothing, but it is the celestial band of star signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Zodiacal means relating to the zodiac, the band of constellations including Capricorn.

clue.text: Time to 'show such antagonism?

clue.text: Subject getting to elect no king

indicators.note: no king means the letter standing for king is dropped from the chosen word

parts.note: to elect is to pick

explanation.surface: A subject of a monarchy is asked to vote, but there is no monarch on the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Quake producing extremes of terror. over capital

indicators.note: extremes of means take just the first and last letters of the word terror
over in a down clue means the city name is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An earthquake brings the edges of fear across a city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' turns the city upside down; 'capital' could tempt as money or a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a small earthquake or shaking of the ground.

clue.text: Spicy sort of literary miscellany?

definitions.meaning: a scented mixture of dried petals and spices kept in a bowl
a medley or collection of assorted writings or pieces

explanation.definitionFit: Pot-pourri is both a fragrant mix of petals and spices and a mixed collection of works.

clue.text: Friend's exclamation immediately after entering

indicators.note: entering means the time phrase goes inside the shout word

parts.note: a cry is an exclamation
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A pal shouts as soon as he comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend's' is 'Friend is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close friend or companion.

clue.text: Modified training received by female journalist

indicators.note: received by means the exercise abbreviation is taken in between the other two pieces

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
ED is short for editor, a journalist
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A woman reporter takes in some exercise and is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage PT is the school subject physical training; 'received by' puts it between the girl's name and the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapted means altered to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Conductor in English tram's unusually old

indicators.note: unusually means the gathered letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: A conductor rides an English tram that is strangely antiquated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a tram conductor, but it is the leader of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor.

clue.text: House left by German king

parts.note: Otto I was a German king and Holy Roman Emperor

explanation.surface: A building is abandoned by a German monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is not a building but the British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, which is also called house.

clue.text: Collected writings presenting a new religious doctrine out East

indicators.note: out means the compass letter is left out of the study of religion

parts.note: theology is the study of religious doctrine

explanation.surface: Collected texts present a fresh faith that has left the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes an E from THEOLOGY, giving THOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a published collection of poems or other pieces.

clue.text: Religious type from Yale straying in all directions

indicators.note: straying means the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west and south give N, E, W and S

explanation.surface: A believer from an American university wanders all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges YALE together with NEWS, the four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wesleyan is a Methodist, a follower of John Wesley.

clue.text: Was ordered by unknown individual to settle in African country

indicators.note: ordered means the three letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
I is the first-person individual
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: Someone is told by a stranger to put down roots in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges WAS to SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaziland, now Eswatini, is a kingdom in southern Africa.

clue.text: Roguish principal in combinations

definitions.meaning: as a prefix it means chief

explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly mischievous, and as a prefix it marks the chief of a kind.

clue.text: Exhorted converts to accept nothing schismatic

indicators.note: to accept means the scrambled letters take the round letter inside
converts means the letters of the word before it are changed into a new form

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A preacher urges new believers to take nothing on trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers, but it is the anagram signal on EXHORTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox means departing from accepted belief, as a schismatic group does.

clue.text: Soldier mostly going round with senior bureaucrat

indicators.note: going round means the shortened soldier word encloses the joining word
mostly means the fighting man word loses its last letter

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving on ships
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A soldier circles about in the company of a top civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the soldier's last letter, and 'going round' makes what is left enclose the joining word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful senior civil servant, after the officials of imperial China.

clue.text: Old aunt, originally in Eccles, changing fuse

indicators.note: changing means the pooled letters are altered into a new order
originally means only the starting letter of aunt is used

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester, famous for its currant cakes

explanation.surface: An elderly aunt from a Lancashire town is changing a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like an electrical part, but it is the verb meaning merge.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to come together and merge into one.

clue.text: Attack lecher

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means set upon; as a noun it is slang for a lustful man.

clue.text: It's dodgy on stormy ocean for one

definitions.text: It's dodgy on stormy ocean for one

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the second piece follows the first
stormy means the sea word is tossed about into a new order
dodgy means the letters of the first word are shifted around

explanation.surface: Being out on a rough sea is a risky business for a paddler.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'stormy' shuffles the sea word into the boat, 'dodgy' shuffles the first word, and 'on' places it after.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler of a small craft would find rough sea dangerous, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Vessel goes round island for pleasure trip

indicators.note: goes round means the container word encircles the single letter

parts.note: a cruse is an old word for a small pot or jar

explanation.surface: A ship circles an island on a holiday voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a CRUSE, an earthenware jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a sea voyage taken for pleasure.

clue.text: Raise weapon and secure something small but valuable

indicators.note: Raise in a down clue means the firearm word is lifted upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to get is to obtain or secure

explanation.surface: Lift your rifle and grab a precious prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump of gold, or anything small and precious.

clue.text: Collection taken by party official is complete

parts.note: a whip enforces discipline among a party's MPs
round can mean complete, as in a round dozen

explanation.surface: A party enforcer passes the hat and finishes the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A WHIP is the British parliamentary official who keeps party members voting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money among colleagues.

clue.text: Mollusc ends off shell in' seven days

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word sits inside the abbreviation for a week

parts.note: WK is the abbreviation for week, seven days

indicators.note: ends off means the first and last letters are removed from the word shell

explanation.surface: A sea creature loses the edges of its shell within a week.
explanation.walkthrough: HEL, from 'shell' with 'ends off', goes 'in' WK.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelk is a sea snail with a spiral shell.

clue.text: Witty remark one let drop in this vessel

indicators.note: let drop means the number word is removed from the front of the joke word

parts.note: a one-liner is a short witty remark
taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke is told and dropped aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let drop' takes ONE from ONE-LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship.

clue.text: Head entertaining a bishop is person of great wealth

indicators.note: entertaining means the head word holds the other letters inside, as a host does guests

parts.note: nob is slang for head
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A leader hosting a cleric turns out to be very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very rich man, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: Flower to be got from girl-friend

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
bud is slang for a friend, short for buddy

explanation.surface: A flower can be had from a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower to be' is a witty definition: a bud is a flower not yet open.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an unopened rose, a future bloom.

clue.text: Docked gently, using this sort of anchor

indicators.note: using means the answer is made from letters taken from inside the words docked gently

explanation.surface: A boat docked gently with the help of a certain anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedge is a small anchor used to warp a ship along.

clue.text: Touchy person can fight about article in' German

indicators.note: about means the can and fight words are placed around the German article

parts.note: a tin is a can
to box is to fight
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: An irritable man can fight over a piece of German writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is a grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox is something or someone ready to flare up at a spark.
